content.rationale:
This decision is the landing modelled as a machine artifact, and every element it carries is one of the four prerequisites' facts stated in the record's own terms. `specs/drafts/land.qnt` is one Quint module in the house form of `specs/drafts/state.qnt`, `open.qnt`, `guard.qnt` and `drift.qnt`: it imports `draft_state`, steps only the registry variable `records`, and declares no variable of its own.

The comparison is zsvukpls and ptlmptoy. zsvukpls fixes the base the opening recorded as one entry for every path of the owned set, each the identity of that path's content, and leaves the identity's encoding open; through tvtnokzu the record carries it as `base: str -> Identity`, so the module compares the opaque identities with the type's own equality and chooses no algorithm, length or textual form. ptlmptoy fixes the comparison the landing makes: the base against the owned set as it stands, path by path, a differing path being one on which the two sides disagree in either direction, including a base entry the owned set no longer holds and an owned path the base does not carry. `differsAt` and `differing` state exactly that symmetric difference over the union of the two key sets, and `stale` is ptlmptoy's `no longer matches` read as `at least one differing path`. The owned set's content is not registry state — it is read from jj at the landing — so it enters as the `now: str -> Identity` input of each step rather than as a second variable, and the module never re-reads or rewrites a record's base.

Selection is tvtnokzu's record: the handle is the key a record is filed under, so a landing addresses exactly one record and the handle alone picks it out, not the record's node, its edit, its workspace, or a path a call names. `refuseUnknown` is that fact read as a refusal: a handle the registry does not hold addresses no record, so the step places nothing and leaves every record as it was. The node is read only by the stale test below — to select which records name the addressed record's node, never to select which record the landing acts on — so two records naming the same node stay two records and only the one whose handle is addressed can move.

The node-wide test is ptlmptoy with uvrltuvo, reached through vmwvnnzv. ptlmptoy refuses a stale landing and names `each stale draft` by its handle and the differing paths; uvrltuvo, recorded beneath vmwvnnzv, states the rule the model must carry: an open record naming the target node that is stale refuses the landing even when the source is a different, current record, and the refusal names each stale handle with the paths that differ for it. The target node is the node the addressed record names, so `staleHandlesOn` selects the records that are `open` — the state value tvtnokzu carries — and whose single `node` field equals that node, and asks `stale` of each one's base; `nodeStale` is that set being non-empty. The addressed record's own freshness is therefore necessary but not sufficient: `land` is enabled only when `nodeStale` is false, and `refuseStale` is enabled when it holds and the addressed record is open, so a fresh addressed record is still refused while any open record on the same node is stale. The test fixes which records it ranges over — open records naming the target node — and neither an order among them nor a cap on how many there are.

The refusal is ptlmptoy and uvrltuvo. `refusal` maps each stale open handle on that node to its differing paths, one entry per stale record because one landing refuses on behalf of every stale draft naming the node, not only the one it addressed. The order of the handles and of the paths, the separators, the wording, the stream and the exit status are all left unfixed, as ptlmptoy leaves them; `refuseStale` is that refusal as a step that leaves `records` exactly as it stood, so nothing is placed, no state moves and no base is rewritten.

`land` is vmwvnnzv's fresh landing: subject to the node-wide test, when no open record naming the addressed record's node is stale, exactly the addressed record is replaced by the state module's `landed` form (tvtnokzu), which keeps its handle, its three references and its base as filed, so the record is retained and every other record — including a stale sibling the refusal would have named — is untouched. That is the model's only state move, `open` to `landed`: `land` requires the record to be open and no definition writes a state back, so a landed record is not landed again and none is reversed. That the placement of the changed owned paths into the node's change and the record's turn happen inside one recording is the operation boundary vmwvnnzv already names, and not a registry fact, so the module models one step and adds no operation, marker or bracket: it neither places a path nor represents the placement, and it holds nothing about the document a record is read from, its path, its filename or its encoding.

The module therefore adds no operation and no storage fact. Its only variable is the record registry the state module already declares; its steps are the landing, its two refusals and the composition of the three; and its pure definitions read the registry and the input owned set and write nothing. Everything a prerequisite leaves open — the refusal's shape and delivery, the timing of the read, how a handle is minted, how the source resolves to an edit, how `--to` agrees with the record's node, the placement itself and the recording's undo — stays open, and the model constrains none of it.

What this refine changes, and why. The earlier form of this module tested only the record the handle addresses and named only that record: `refusal` took one record, and `land` and `refuseStale` asked `stale` of the addressed record's base alone. That read ptlmptoy as a per-record rule and left a landing with a fresh source free to land while an open sibling naming the same node was stale — exactly the case ptlmptoy's `each stale draft` and uvrltuvo's node-wide sentence refuse. This refine replaces the per-record test with `staleHandlesOn` and `nodeStale` over the addressed record's node, makes `refusal` a map over every stale handle on that node, guards `land` with the node-wide test and enables `refuseStale` when it holds, so the addressed record's freshness is necessary but not sufficient. Nothing else changes: the comparison, the selection by handle, the refusal leaving the registry as it stood, the single `open`-to-`landed` move, the retention, the untouched siblings, the step composition, the single stepped variable and every exclusion stay as they were.
